Sums and Products Invariant

InvariantsArithmeticAlgorithms
Game: Merge pairs of numbers until one is left — and predict that last number in advance.
How to play: Click two numbers to replace them by their product plus both of them. Repeat restores the start.

Look for the math

You can know the last number before making a single move. The secret is to add one to every number.

The operation in disguise

Replacing A and B by A·B + A + B is the same as replacing them by (A+1)(B+1) − 1. The product of all the numbers increased by one therefore loses the two factors (A+1) and (B+1) and gains exactly their product. Nothing changes.

Reading the invariant

So P = ∏(Aᵢ + 1) − 1 is an invariant. When one number is left it must equal P. For the page's list 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 that is 7! − 1 = 5039, whatever order you merge in. The logic test checks every possible move on all lists of three small numbers and 400 random longer lists.

What happens if one of the numbers is 0? What if all of them are −1?

Puzzle by Alexander Bogomolny (cut-the-knot.org)
